title: TinyTS: Memory-Efficient TinyML Model Compiler Framework on Microcontrollers
problem: Deploying DNNs on MCUs is constrained by limited SRAM; layer-wise allocation causes out-of-memory exceptions for large tensors, while patch-based inference reduces memory but significantly increases inference time due to redundant computation.
motivation: Enabling efficient neural network deployment on memory-constrained microcontrollers is essential for edge ML applications.
method: TinyTS breaks tensors (neural network data) into smaller pieces using a partitioning method that avoids the redundant recalculations simpler splitting approaches cause. It uses a memory planner that frees storage as soon as pieces aren't needed anymore, cutting peak memory use. It also removes metadata storage and runtime overhead from tracking these pieces. Together, this approach lets neural networks run on memory-limited microcontrollers without wasting computation.
key_novelty: A compiler method that reduces memory by splitting tensors (neural network data) while eliminating the redundant computations that simpler splitting approaches incurred.
contributions: Novel tensor partitioning method eliminating redundant computation in patch-based inference
Memory planner enabling early memory release for unused split tensors to reduce peak SRAM
Optimization techniques for metadata and runtime overhead reduction
Achieves up to 5.92X peak SRAM reduction and 8.83X speedup over baseline approaches

metrics.other: 5.92X peak SRAM reduction over TFLM baseline
